summary: Scope LeanPool/@subtrees/3 grew from 61 previously reviewed files to 655 files across 15 vendored LeanPool projects (HopfProblem 146, ClassificationOfSurfaces 132, Schoenflies 130, Feige 88, Malliavin 57, RiemannRochFunctionFields 36, CencovPetz 24, DemazureProduct 11, Flean 7, PCFTheory 6, FoZfc 6, Desargues 4, ConcentrationInequalities 4, Erdos403 3, LongGapsBetweenPrimes 1). All 655 listed paths resolve in the checkout with byte sizes equal to the brief. A declaration-keyword grep over the full scope found 3 files with no theorem/lemma/def/structure/class/instance/inductive/abbrev/example/axiom/elab/noncomputable match: PCFTheory/Background.lean, RiemannRochFunctionFields/Genus.lean, and RiemannRochFunctionFields/WeilDifferential.lean. All 3 were read in full and are pure module-import indexes (module header, public import of sibling submodules plus at most one Mathlib import, a docstring, and in one case `@[expose] public section`). Malliavin/Malliavin.lean matched the grep only through its own name in import paths; read in full, it is also a pure import index of three Malliavin submodules plus a provenance comment. These 4 files are retained: under FILTER-007 and the current FD-016 state, verified import-only modules stay primary-eligible and are ranked with the navigation-import-only role, not filtered, which matches the precedent in the other units of this source. CencovPetz/Basic.lean (355 bytes, second smallest) was read in full; it has an empty `namespace LeanPool.CencovPetz ... end` block, a namespace command that takes it outside FILTER-007's unilateral class, and it is the declared root module of the Cencov-Petz package, so it is retained. The largest files (HopfProblem/Recognition/Smale6.lean 321697 bytes, Degree2.lean 318381 bytes) are dense proof files with 260 and 153 top-level declarations. The largest table-named file, DemazureProduct/Tableaux.lean (46084 bytes), holds 53 top-level declarations on linked sets of integer pairs. One representative file per project directory has real declarations. The junk-signal and TODO/FIXME greps found only ordinary mathematical prose, hypothesis names, and developer notes on real proofs. No file lacks formal mathematical content relevant to search, so every file is retained.
